issues.description: The problem statement and the UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters (returns String like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the template/Main usage also calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments. The solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implements it in Goat and Seal), which introduces a parameter that contradicts the specification and the intended usage. This mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature and prevents straightforward implementation of the interface as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API across all artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to match the problem: change Milkable.messageOnMilk(double) to messageOnMilk() returning String and adjust Seal/Goat implementations to return the exact phrasing "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (no volume), or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnMilk(double volume) (and document the expected return format including the volume). The preferred fix is (A) to preserve the exercise wording and the UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters that returns a String like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". The solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (a different signature) and implementations include the volume in the returned string. This signature mismatch between problem/template and solution will confuse students (and causes the template's example call m.messageOnMilk() to be invalid against the solution API).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API across artifacts. Either (A) change solution's Milkable to 'String messageOnMilk()' and update Seal/Goat implementations to return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (no volume), matching the UML/problem/template; or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and template Main.java examples to require 'messageOnMilk(double volume)' and document the volume parameter consistently.
